articleTitle: Land Use Land Cover Classification using Deep Learning Techniques: A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: Land Use and Land Cover (LULC) maps serve as an important component for natural resource monitoring. They convey insights into the utilization patterns of the Earth’s land surface and the various forms of coverage present therein. In this research, we evaluated the performance of different deep learning architectures in the segmentation of satellite images into six distinct land cover classes such as trees, cropland, water bodies, built-up areas, roads and barren land. A unique dataset was curated utilizing Microsoft Bing Satellite imagery, encompassing the distinct land use classes within a region situated in the Mandya district, Karnataka. The digitization process was conducted using QGIS, facilitating the preparation of training and evaluation data for the development of trained Deep Learning (DL) models using popular DL architectures namely, FCN, U-Net, PSP, and DeeplabV3+. The performance of these models was compared with respect to their Fl score and mean Intersection of Union(mloU) metrics, on test datasets. From the comparison, it was observed that U-Net with ResNet-34 as the backbone demonstrated the best performance with a Mean IoU score of 0.803 and an overall Fl score of 0.89 on the test set. The generalization capability of the models was also evaluated by applying them to larger geographical areas, demonstrating their potential for Land Use Land Cover mapping for large areas.

articleTitle: Cyclic Heap Permutation Based Reconfiguration of Solar PV Array for Optimal Shade Dispersion
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: Partial shading poses a critical challenge to optimizing the performance of photovoltaic (PV) systems, affecting the attainment of maximum power output and overall system efficiency. Inadequate management of partial shading conditions (PSCs) can threaten the stability and effectiveness of PV systems. This study presents an innovative reconfiguration approach grounded in a cyclic heap permutation strategy, to alleviate the detrimental effects of Partial Shading Conditions (PSCs). Through the strategic redistribution of shading effects, the proposed reconfiguration method improves the efficiency of PV systems across a spectrum of shading scenarios. Rigorous performance evaluations, considering various shading cases and configurations, reveal the efficacy of the proposed cyclic heap permutation-based reconfiguration technique. We also highlight its versatility and adaptability across different PV array sizes and shading conditions. This study adds to continuous endeavors aimed at fortifying the resilience and improving the efficiency of solar PV systems confronted with partial shading challenges.

articleTitle: Optimizing Stock Market Predictions: A Comprehensive 3-Stage Model with Residual Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: We present a novel three-stage model that leverages residual modeling techniques to forecast time series in financial markets. To evaluate the model’s performance, we use a comprehensive set of seven financial indexes covering approximately 2272 trading days for each index, including 453 days for testing. Our results show that our proposed model consistently outperforms the reservoir computing (RC) model, which has previously demonstrated superior performance to deep learning models. Our proposed model is more accurate making it an ideal solution for time-series forecasting.

articleTitle: LiNbO3 Crystal Characterization for Advanced RF Sensing Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: The manuscript provides a study focused on the basic characterization of Lithium niobate (LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) crystals, particularly their electro-optic sensing behavior and response to DC and phase variations under RF microwave fields at 15GHz. The work introduces the proposed idea of utilizing LiNbO3 crystals for advanced RF sensing applications, such as vector E-field probe and antenna design, SAR measurements, and vector SAR analysis at higher frequencies.

articleTitle: FISmark: Heritage Image Copyright Protection with FIS based Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: Cultural images (CI) are the basis of our important heritage sites present on this earth. CI symbolic highlights for the culture and tradition which our society inherent it. Since the dissemination of CI is growing at a vital pace so their integrity needs to be protected from unauthorized users. In this proposed technique a novel image watermarking technique is designed for copyright protection of CI. Initially in this approach a hybrid watermark image is generated using CI and its geographical location with the aid of lifting wavelet transform (LWT), singular value decomposition (SVD), secure hash algorithm (SHA-384). The watermarking is performed out in YCbCr color domain using redundant discrete wavelet transform (RDWT), randomized singular value decomposition (RSVD) and fuzzy inference system (FIS) optimization technique. The role of FIS is to compute the value of embedding factor so that performance of proposed watermarking technique is strengthen. Several performance metrics are computed for the proposed technique which highlights for the efficiency as compared to other existing techniques.

articleTitle: Assessing YOLOv8 as a Classifier for Detection of Synthetically Generated Facial Imagery
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: The literature has shown that facial recognition technology has been widely employed in diverse industries, such as consumer and security applications. It played a crucial role in enhancing consumer security measures, facilitating biometric identification processes, and elevating consumer experiences. However, the deployment of this technology also leads to significant privacy and ethical considerations that necessitate meticulous attention and regulation in operations. In recent years, You Only Look Once (YOLO) has also shown promising results as an image classifier. However, an in-depth analysis is required to explore the effectiveness of YOLOv8 in the classification of real and fake facial images. Hence, this research is to build an image classification framework employing the YOLOv8 architecture with the aim of efficiently differentiating between real and fake or synthetic (artificially generated) facial images. The methodology involves training the YOLOv8 model using a publicly accessible dataset containing both real and fake faces generated using generative artificial intelligence (AI). The dataset has been obtained from the Kaggle database, consisting of 140k real and fake images employing AI. The extensive series of experimental findings validates the efficacy of the model, with a notable training and testing accuracy of 99.35% and 98.2%, respectively. These significant results are obtained with training over 20 epochs with a minimal error rate of 0.0065. The aforementioned results are the best among standalone deep learning models trained using transfer learning, highlighting the practical efficiency and resilience of the proposed framework for discerning authentic and AI generated facial images, hence demonstrating its potential for use in diverse practical contexts.

articleTitle: Human Speech Extraction from Composite Audio Signal in Real-Time using Deep Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: Studies indicate that humans have the exceptional capability to focus on speech even in environments with complex background noises. To create a computational equivalent of this ability, recent studies have focused on developing speech extraction algorithms. These algorithms aim to extract human speech signals from a mixture of overlapping background sounds. In this paper, efforts are made to utilize the novel encoder-decoder neural network architecture to accomplish this task for real-time and streaming applications. The training of the model involved utilizing synthetic 6-second single-channel composite audio mixtures generated from three distinct datasets using the Scaper toolkit. Our results showcase an impressive SI-SNRi of 14.209 and a latency of 874 ms, obtained on a consumer-grade Intel Quad-Core i5 processor with default multithreading. The obtained outcomes provide compelling evidence for the feasibility and efficacy of the proposed approach, establishing a strong proof-of-concept for the real-world application of the model. Streaming human speech extraction could revolutionize acoustic applications for headphones, hearing aids, and telephony.

articleTitle: Analyzing Muscle Synergies for Finger Movement Recognition using sEMG Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: The study focuses on extracting muscle synergy from electromyographic (EMG) signals for recognition of finger movement. The process involves using a non-negative matrix factorization (NNMF) technique to decompose the EMG signal matrix into muscle synergies and their corresponding activation coefficients. The synergy obtained from this process reveals the underlying patterns in the EMG data that help in the classification of finger movements. Other steps include hyperparameter tuning using grid search, feature selection using sequential forward selection (SFS), and classification using support vector machine (SVM). The proposed method shows the effectiveness of NNMF in detecting muscle synergy for accurate classification of finger movements. A classification accuracy of 97.5±1.67% is obtained.

articleTitle: An ultrathin compact orientation insensitive chipless RFID tag with high bit capacity.
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: Radiofrequency identification (RFID) technology has been gaining traction in various industries for its applications in identification and tracking. Lately, there has been a growing interest in chipless RFID tags due to their cost-effectiveness and wide-ranging utility. Among the innovations in this domain, orientation-independent chipless RFID tags are emerging as promising solutions for future sensing devices. The primary objective of this paper is to investigate the adaptability of chipless RFID tags, specifically in terms of their resistance to rotation. The second objective is to attain high coding capacity simultaneously. The research delves into using octagonal resonators to achieve orientation-independent properties in the tag. The design of the chipless RFID tag employs an octagonal resonator pattern on a 0.15 mm-thick FR-4 substrate with an overall size of 22 x 22mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The proposed tag comprises eleven concentric octagonal resonators, and the study also explores its potential for high bit-capacity applications.

articleTitle: A Compact, Dual-Band Pentagon Shaped Planar Antenna for 28/38 GHz 5G Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: This paper presents a dual-band pentagon double-ring loaded patch antenna, demonstrating effective operation in two distinct millimeter wave (mm-Wave) bands 28/38 GHz with a bandwidth of 17.80% & 6.46%. The gain of the proposed antenna is 3.92/4.57 dBi with radiation efficiency greater than 92% over the entire band of operation. The antenna is designed with precision using Rogers RT5880 substrate with a thickness of 0.508 mm & a relative permittivity of 2.2. This design represents a simple design approach for creating a dual-band and compact planar antenna for millimeter-wave 5G communication.

articleTitle: Crop Prediction from Soil Parameters using Light Ensemble Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: Agriculture has emerged as a significant source of paychecks for many nations that are developing. The agricultural community in these countries has numerous kinds of issues, including climate change, nutrient deficiencies, and crop rotations. Machine learning has emerged as a dynamic tool in agriculture for tackling such obstacles and propelling harvest efficiency. Algorithms supporting machine learning have been successful in forecasting the best supplies for farmers by taking into account numerous factors. The study integrates algorithm-supporting machine learning to varied data sets in the framework of crop production prediction issues, grading soil parameters such as rainfall, temperature, humidity, pH levels, nitrogen (N), phosphorous (P), and potassium (K). A profound connection has been incorporated through this comprehensive research, allowing for accurate predictions in the ever-changing agrarian sector: The ensemble learning technique which is known as the light gradient boosting machine (Light GBM) algorithm, which predicted an accuracy rate of 99%, is implemented in the proposed method. This proposed method will be a helping hand for farmers to get better yields.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of IRS-Assisted Wireless Communication in Presence of Single and Multiple Eavesdroppers
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: In this work, we analyze the error performance and the security performance of intelligent reflecting surface (IRS)-assisted wireless communication systems. In particular, a single-antenna transmitter sends information signals to a single-antenna receiver via IRS in the presence of single and multiple eavesdroppers. It is assumed that the channel state information (CSI) of the transmitter-to-IRS’s and IRS-to-receiver’s channels is perfectly known to the IRS. We investigate the performance of optimized IRS based transmission in terms of bit error rate (BER) as well as secrecy capacity considering Rayleigh fading. The simulation results demonstrate that optimized IRS based transmission scheme appreciably enhances the BER and the secrecy capacity of the designed system compared to the blind transmission scheme. Furthermore, our results show that with the increase in number of reflecting elements, the BER and secrecy capacity improves.

articleTitle: Enhancing Accuracy in Doppler Frequency Shift Estimation and Velocity Measurement for Doppler Velocity Log Applications: A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: This research examines the prominent role of sonar technology, especially the Doppler Velocity Log (DVL), in the determination of ship velocity. The DVL employs a four-beam Janus configuration to measure a ship’s velocity relative to the waterbed by transmitting acoustic pulses along different azimuth-oriented beams. The study focuses on a scenario where a ship moving through a waterbed produces a Doppler frequency shift, a critical parameter for determining the ship velocity. This paper presents a thorough comparison between the correlation-based broad-band pulse-pair method and the narrow-band least squares method for the determination of Doppler frequency shift. The selection of these methods dynamically adapts to varying water depths. The algorithms are developed and simulated in MATLAB, followed by implementation in Digital Signal Processor (DSP), and further validated through trials in diverse water bodies. Results indicate the broad-band pulse-pair method excelling in low-depth scenarios, while the narrow-band least squares algorithm performs optimally in higher depths. Dynamic algorithm switching based on the water depth exhibits an adaptive approach, enhancing the accuracy of Doppler shift estimations. This study contributes valuable insights for optimizing DVL frequency estimation, providing a practical solution for underwater navigation across varying depth conditions.

articleTitle: ASIC SoC Design for Edge Computing Agriculture Application
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: This paper introduces an ASIC implementation tailored for agriculture applications, leveraging RISC-V for digital processing and sensor interfacing circuits. The design focuses on early plant disease detection and yield improvement. Three sensors for temperature, humidity, and crop wetness are integrated for edge computing, processing data closer to the source. The design includes both analog and digital ASICs, with analog circuits designed based on sensor specifications. Multi-technology node designs and stacking of two ASICs are explored for shorter and denser connections. The RISC core has an area of 50927 $\mu m^{\mathbf{2}}$, critical path delay of 361 ps, and power consumption of 420 pW after placement and routing. The analog ASIC, covering signal processing components, has a combined routed length of 23358 pm and a total area of 2.366 mm2, tested with AMS verification methodology using Cadence CAD tools.

articleTitle: Prognostic Modeling for Heart Failure Survival: A Classification Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: Heart failure kills millions of people globally every year. This work employs a classification-based predictive system utilizing machine learning techniques and provides precise health analysis. The model is evaluated based on the F1 score, accuracy, precision, and confusion matrix. We have obtained an accuracy of 88.33 percent by tuning the appropriate hyperparameter. This research aims to identify the significance of hyperparameter tuning within classification algorithms. The result of this study may potentially make significant changes in the healthcare sector and may also increase the chances of survival of heart failure patients. This study also tries to identify the important features that should be considered while analyzing heart failure survival based on the publicly available dataset. The model has been made easily accessible over a web-based UI interface.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Inspired Classification Model of Different Edible Oil Samples using High Sensitivity Microwave Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: Food safety has received a lot of attention over the recent years, and the quality of cooking oil is very important. Adulteration is very common in edible oils. Studies have been conducted using electromagnetic waves to analyze the properties of materials. Henceforth, the quality of edible oil can be checked by measuring the dielectric constant of the oil sample. Microwave sensors are of great interest due to their superior sensitivity, durability, and affordability. A complementary split ring resonator (CSRR) based compact sensor with high quality factor having dimensions as 15 X 25 X 0.8 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> is designed on Rogers RT-Duroid 5880 substrate with relative permittivity 2.2. The designed sensor shows frequency shift with change in the permittivity of the oil samples used, showing high sensitivity. In this work, a machine learning integrated oil classification approach has also been proposed utilizing the above designed microstrip based sensor. Out of various models used, gradient boosting classifier and naive bayes showed maximum accuracy of almost 96%.

articleTitle: Combinational Distortion Assessment of Laparoscopic Videos using Deep EfficientNet Model
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: Laparoscopic images are susceptible to several distortions making it challenging for surgeons to have a clear visibility of images/videos during surgery. Distortions in images might lead to misdiagnosis, leads to adverse consequences. An objective technique for assessing the laparoscopic image quality is required in order to identify the type of distortion. Most of the laparoscopic image datasets with distortion labels are not publicly available and are limited to certain distortions. Laparoscopic Image Quality Assessment (LAPIQA) dataset is created with the necessary labels specifically for working with this model. It comprises of three distinct distortions blur, smoke/fog and uneven illumination each of which has five levels and can be either a single distortion or combination of distortions. A deep learning based multi-label distortion classification model is implemented to identify the various types of distortions. Modified EfficientNetBO is used with added custom layers and sigmoid activation for the model. The model is trained with both hinge loss and binary cross entropy (BCE) and validated using metrics such as accuracy, loss, precision, recall and f1-score. With respect to accuracy, model yields an average training accuracy of 96.51%, with a training loss of O.55, validation accuracy of 95.85%, with a validation loss of O.57 and testing accuracy of 96.12% with a loss of O.71. The proposed classification approach effectively identifies and evaluates both single and combined distortions in laparoscopic images.

articleTitle: Do Single Beat ECGs have Same Credibility as Continuous ECG Signal in Multi-Class Classification using Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: Artificial intelligence has proven to be a boon for humanity in various field of science, however meaningful results using Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) models depends on various factors. One of the factors is to feed the model with large size datasets. For this purpose, segmentation of ECG into Single Beat ECGs (SB-ECG) has become prominent. This study attempts to investigate whether there is an effect of using SB-ECG compared to the continuous recorded ECGs on the model output. The aim of this work is to examine and compare the effect of single beat and continuous ECGs on the ML model multi-class classification performance. 120 ECGs of Sinus Rhythm (SR), Sinus Tachycardia (ST) and Atrial Tachycardia (AT) recorded for 10 seconds using standard 12 lead were retrieved from online database. Two datasets were prepared of 120 and 1687 samples of continuous ECG and SBECG, respectively. The datasets were fed to the ML model and their performance were evaluated. Extra trees model gave the best performance for both datasets. Continuous ECG recording gave the 10 -fold cross validated data accuracy of 77.36% and SB-ECGs gave 92.97% with Area Under Curve (AUC) score of 88.07 and 98.92 respectively. SB-ECG gave better classification performance than the continuous ECG recording. SB-ECG can be used for enhanced clinical diagnosis with better accuracy and reduced false outcomes. Also, the study on SB-ECG may prove to be highly efficient in paroxysmal atrial fibrillation detection where episodes of arrhythmia are sudden.

articleTitle: Terahertz Regime Dual-Port Tripple-band Microstrip Based MIMO Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: In this study, a novel dual-port rectangular patch antenna is presented that provides triple-band operation across three distinct frequency subranges:15.25-15.6THz, 16.3-18.2THz, and 19.03-19. 7THz.The antenna functions within the frequency range of 15 THz to 20 THz. The findings of the research highlight the antenna's efficient operation of important parameters such as reflection coefficient, VSWR, bandwidth, and gain. Remarkably, the suggested antenna design has many uses. In addition to the previously specified performance metrics, simulated results show that the antenna remains isolated ablest an19dB over the entire operating frequency range, which is additional evidence of its reliable operation and compliance with conventional antenna standards.

articleTitle: Predicting Heartbeats in Real-Time: A Continuous Monitoring Approach with Face Recognition Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: Healthcare practitioners heavily depend on Electrocardiogram (ECG) machines to acquire critical insights into heart function through waveform analysis. The information can be used for monitoring and understanding overall heart health. However, the onset of the Covid-19 pandemic prompted global governments to implement stringent guidelines, emphasizing touchless healthcare methods. To overcome this problem, an innovative and reliable method for continuous heart rate estimation without physical contact has been introduced. The approach leverages face recognition algorithms to predict real-time heart pulse rates based on color intensity measurements. To accommodate inputs from videos or images, a segmentation algorithm is integrated. Rigorous experiments involving volunteers validate the results, revealing relative errors below 6%, a margin widely accepted in the field. The work concludes with a comparative analysis, assessing the proposed approach against existing literature. The system excels in providing a touchless and efficient approach to the crucial task.

articleTitle: Enhancing Early-Stage Breast Cancer Detection: Antenna Design, Realistic Phantom Modeling, and Multi-Static Imaging with DAS Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: This research delves into an exploration of diverse microwave imaging techniques for the early detection of breast cancer (BCD), focusing on the enhancement of detection capabilities through the development of a specialized antenna. The presented work introduces a microstrip inset-fed rectangular microstrip patch antenna with compact dimensions (17.75 x 15.16 x 1.21 mm^3). The design utilizes a RT 6202 substrate (0.51 mm thickness, dielectric constant of 2.94). Furthermore, the study pioneers the creation of a novel breast organ phantom model using CST Studio Suite, aiming to construct a more realistic representation for improved correlation accuracy during clinical practical trials. In the imaging domain, a qualitative multi-static microwave imaging approach is adopted, employing the Delay and Sum (DAS) algorithm implemented in MATLAB. This methodology enables the detection and localization of designed tumors within the breast model, facilitating potential advancements in early-stage breast cancer diagnosis.

articleTitle: Models for Exploring the Benefits of using Discrete Wavelet Transformation in HSI
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: The application of Hyper Spectral Images is increasing day-by-day, with the development of remote sensing technology. With the rapid development of Deep Learning technology, many research work focus on Classification of Hyper Spectral Images based on both spectral and spatial features extraction. It is the task of correctly predicting the class values of different pixel values present in remotely sensed HSI data. In order to achieve the accurate classification of ground features, Feature Extraction is one of the crucial step which increases the accuracy of learned models by extracting relevant features from the input data. As the HSI image consists of hundreds of continuous spectral bands, we need an effective way to extract the spectral features of the HSI images (other than CNN techniques). In this paper, we exploit two different types of Discrete wavelet transformation techniques like Haar, Daubechies (Db4) for spectral feature extraction. This in turn reduces the dimensionality of data. These spectral features are then linked to four layers of 2D CNN to extract the spatial features. The extracted features from the wavelet fusion CNN are provided further for classification. Initially factor Analysis method was used to reduce the dimensions of the HSI input data. Our experimental results conclude the better accuracy method among these, through a comparative analysis with other state-of-the-art methods. We use Overall Accuracy, Kappa Coefficient and Average Accuracy as a Performance measures on 3 benchmark datasets of Indian Pines, Salina Scene, University of Pavia.

articleTitle: Emotion Recognition in Speech Using MFCC and Energy Based Ratio Features
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: Emotion recognition from speech signal has emerged as a prominent research focus within the realm of human computer interaction in the last decade. Nonetheless, the existing recognition accuracy requires enhancement. To improve the recognition accuracy the proposed framework adopts a global feature extraction approach, decomposing the input speech signal into Intrinsic Mode Functions (IMFs). After that, the Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC), and energy-based ratio features are extracted from each IMF. The ReliefF algorithm is employed to select pertinent features, which are subsequently tested on an optimizable ensemble classifier for evaluation. The proposed method provides 95.3% emotion recognition accuracy.

articleTitle: Design of triangular MIMO antenna for 5G and beyond
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: In this paper, design and simulation of high frequency antennas for 5G and beyond 5G have been proposed and investigated. This new era of 5G and beyond 5G are useful to connect most of the available devices and create a proper balance between systems and users as per demand of technology and requirement. For that purpose, a large bandwidth is supposed to be required with better gain. Hence, microwave frequency region 8 to 10 GHz has been explored for 5G and also 7 to 20 GHz is being explored for beyond 5G that is why both possibilities have been taken here. FR4 has been used as substrate material having capability of operating at both low and high frequency and also copper has been used for base material for design triangular shape array MIMO structure to achieve high gain. Structure is simulated with the help of CST microwave studio complete ground. Results obtained from these designs are -14.5dBi, -13.9dBi, 14.3dBi, 13.3dBi for all four ports excited separately or simultaneously. The S11 parameter is -72.82dB for frequency 9.3086GHz. Similar procedure has been used to simulate the single triangular structure with partial ground with gain of 10.5dBi. Few literatures survey has been discussed with evolution of beyond 5G technology. Also merit and demerit have been discussed for proposed structures. Bandwidth is increased from 0.29 GHz to 0.32 GHz. As many designed have already been discussed in section I and II, the new thing which is being introduced in this paper, a simple design, easy fabrication, low loss as it has no slots, available materials with simple feeding techniques.

articleTitle: Real time Gesture Recognition using Improved YOLOv5 Model
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: Hand gesture recognition is part of the study of natural human-computer interaction. The objective of research in gesture recognition is to train computers to recognize and respond appropriately to human hand gestures. You Only Look Once (YOLO), is a deep learning model that is mostly used in the field of computer vision for real time object detection. YOLOv5 is an enhanced version of the YOLO algorithm, which is renowned for its fast and accurate object detection capabilities. This research paper explores the application of YOLOv5 architecture for real-time gesture recognition. The efficient architecture of YOLOv5 is utilized to detect and classify real time human hand gestures accurately and rapidly. A fine-tuned version of the YOLOv5 model is proposed that improves the performance of YOLOv5 with better results. Experimental performance shows that the proposed YOLOv5 model achieves a Mean average precision (mAP) value of 96.8% for real-time performance on a custom dataset of hand gestures. We evaluate our method on a custom-made dataset that outperforms state-of-the-art results.

articleTitle: Empowering Facial Analytics: A Unified Approach for Emotion, Age, Gender and Object Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: This research revolutionizes real-time video analysis by seamlessly integrating emotion, age, gender, and object detection in each frame of a live video feed. The framework leverages a unified deep model that combines pre-trained feature extraction models with CNN architecture, each meticulously trained on specialized datasets tailored to its recognition task. The proposed model achieves commendable accuracy of 85.28% in emotion recognition using FER-2013 dataset, 84% in age estimation, and 88.67% in gender classification using UTK-Face dataset, and 90.81% in object recognition leveraging the Fruits and Vegetables dataset. Moreover, the emotion, gender and object models achieved an average precision of 0.865, recall of 0.866 and F-score of 0.864, while age model achieved a mean squared error of 0.1136, quantitatively showcasing the model performance.

articleTitle: FPGA-Optimized Two-Term Karatsuba Multiplications for Large Integer Multiplications
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: The demand for efficient large integer polynomial multiplications in present day crypto-systems is the need of the hour. Karatsuba-like multiplication is one of the most efficient multiplication algorithm discussed in this work. However, this algorithm is mostly practically avoided due to the presence of complex sub-multiplications at the intermediate steps of computation. Thus, efforts has been made to implement two-term Karatsuba Multiplication (Method-I & Method-II), i.e., TTKM-I and TTKM-II in terms of speed and hardware utilization. The overall performance of the proposed design methods are also noted by calculating Area-Time-Product (ATP) and compared with conventional two-term Karatsuba multiplication (CTTKM) and existing state-of-the-art. Hardware implementations of both the proposed TTKM multiplication architectures are done using Virtex-7 FPGA device in Xilinx ISE platform. Compared with other state-of-the-art designs the performance of the proposed two-term Karatsuba multiplication (Method-I) based on ΔATP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> is 11.108%, 98.686%, 15.561%, 72.012%, 95.122%. 6.009% and 24.601% better than Direct Multiplication (DM), Karat-suba Direct Multiplication (KDM), Karatsuba Comba Multiplication (KCM), Traditional Schoolbook Multiplication (Traditional SBM), SBM-I, SBM-II and CTTKM respectively for 512-bit inputs. Similarly the performance of the proposed two-term Karatsuba multiplication (Method-II) based on ΔATP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> is 1.790%, 98.544%, 6.407%, 68.978%. 94.593% and 16.427% better than Direct Multiplication (DM), Karatsuba Direct Multiplication (KDM), Karatsuba Comba Multiplication (KCM), Traditional SBM, SBM-I, SBM-II, CTTKM respectively for 512-bit inputs. However comparing both the proposed methods of TTKM (Method-I and Method-II), it can be inferred that TTKM-I is 9.780% better than TTKM-II thus proving its area-time-product efficiency.

articleTitle: Design of Multi-Manifold Soft Pneumatic Actuator for Differential Pressures and Improved Control
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: Soft Pneumatics is a sub-branch of Soft Robotics. The research in this field relies on designing and developing new actuators that can be employed for varied range of applications. Design of Soft Pneumatic Actuator (SPA) frequently relies on single chamber or single manifold actuators. SPA designed with a single pressure source can produce customized motion but only in a single direction. This paper proposes a soft pneumatic actuator with multiple manifolds that can employ selective and differential pressure actuation to exhibit better control. The actuator was designed keeping in mind two-way actuation with chamber separation. Even though the chambers lie on the same side they are connected to different manifolds having different pressures. To achieve the desired bending curvature, different actuation sequences can be used in conjunction. A Conical Dome Shape internal chamber design was chosen to avoid excessive ballooning and reduce stresses on the lateral walls. The said actuator employs easy manufacturing techniques and has a wide range of applications. This article discusses the process of designing, analysing, and fabricating an actuator that uses selective actuation.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Wilms tumor images using Generative Adversarial Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: Wilms tumor or Nephroblastoma is paediatric cancer, that can be treated if diagnosed at an early stage. However, no appropriate image dataset is publicly available except the Wilms MRI dataset of Mathematical Image Analysis Group, Saarland University, Germany, which only contain 28 multisequence MR scans. As, huge amount of data is required to train a machine or deep learning model, image synthesis could be beneficial. The absence of professionals who can label data was another problem. In order to meet the data requirements two different Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) - Wasserstein GAN (WGAN) and Pix2Pix GAN have been utilized. These GAN architectures generate high-quality and realistic MRI images in terms critical evaluation metrics. These architectures may potentially benefit the detection of rare diseases which lack sufficient size of medical datasets. With the help of image synthesis and precise amount of data, effective computer-aided diagnostic models could be developed.

articleTitle: ConvNet Model Evaluation for Binary and Multilabel Breast Mammogram Mass Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: Breast mass segmentation in mammograms is a vital step in breast cancer screening. Convolution neural networks (ConvNets) based models have been widely used to segment the breast mass from mammograms, which can be further classified into either benign or malignant. Recently, end-to-end frameworks have been proposed to perform breast mass segmentation and classification in one stage. In this study, we assess the performance of common binary and multi-label segmentation models designed for one-stage mass segmentation and classification tasks. It is important to note that previous investigations predominantly confined their training and testing to abnormal mammograms, those displaying mass abnormality. Furthermore, their evaluation metrics primarily revolved around the degree of spatial overlap between model predictions and ground truth, commonly quantified using the Dice score. However, in the context of a clinically feasible end-to-end framework, the model must be equipped to process both normal and abnormal mammograms as input, necessitating a more comprehensive evaluation strategy. Thus, In the presented work, we aimed to evaluate the binary and multilabel segmentation frameworks concerning end-to-end breast mass segmentation on a private dataset recently prepared by authors. For training, we employed U-Net variants, introducing the False Positive Rate (FPR) alongside the Dice score for performance evaluation. Furthermore, We used information regarding the class of masses (benign or malignant) and breast tissue density provided with each mammogram to analyze the segmentation model’s performance with respect to these parameters.

articleTitle: Multi-Disease Identification in Single Citrus Leaf Image Using Sigmoid Activation and Optimised Threshold
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: Disease classification in plant leaf images for early detection and prevention using deep learning techniques has been largely focused upon recently. Nevertheless, identifying multiple diseases in a single leaf image is still unexplored. Bounding box predictions using object detection techniques have been employed for this purpose. However, such information is not always readily available. This study focuses on identification of multiple diseases in a single leaf image of citrus fruits using state-of-the-art deep learning techniques. The considered leaves have been infected with none, one, two or all three severe diseases – Anthracnose, Melanose, and Bacterial Brown Spot. The probabilities of occurrence of these diseases are predicted for each leaf image using a sigmoid activation layer and a threshold value has been used to decide on whether the disease is present or absent in the leaf. The threshold value has been optimised during the training time using the meta-heuristic ant lion optimisation algorithm. The outcomes highlight the superiority of the DenseNet121 architecture in terms of classification accuracy, as it accurately identifies overlapping disease classes present in citrus leaves, achieving 98.6% accuracy with a threshold probability value of 0.284. Following closely, the MobileNetV2 architecture showcase comparable accuracy values, however, requiring significantly less number of training parameters.

articleTitle: Analysis of Wideband Minkowski Fractal Slot-Loaded Micro-machined Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: This research work presents analysis of the effect of micro-machining on the performance parameters of a wideband fractal patch antenna. Finite element method based High Frequency Structure Simulator (HFSS) has been used to design and analyze Micro-machined (MM) patch fractal antenna. An optimized air cavity in FR4 substrate has been created using milling process. The proposed design has shown improvement in reflection coefficient (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>), gain. and efficiency as compared to conventional antenna design. The proposed MM antenna resonates at 2.63 GHz, 3.75 GHz and 5 GHz and has an impedance bandwidth of 104.8%. Micro-machining at all three resonance frequencies increased the antenna gain by 111.5%, 692.8% and 178% and the efficiency by 8.95%, 10.8% and 12.7%, respectively. The proposed antenna is cost effective, and useful for applications such as: Wi-Fi, WiMax, WLAN, radiolocation, sub-6 GHz 5G Communication, and telemetry. After prototyping the proposed design the antenna has been tested, and a good agreement between simulated and measured results have been found. Novelty-Micro-machining has been used successfully to improve the performance parameters of FR4 substrate based fractal patch antenna by overcoming the losses in substrate.

articleTitle: Genetic Algorithm based Optimal Placement of TCSC for Improving Voltage Profile
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: This paper presents optimal placement of thyrisor controlled series compensator (TCSC) to improve voltage profile and thus improve stability of the system. IEEE 30 bus test system is considered for case study. Newton-Raphson method is applied for load flow analysis. The optimal location of TCSC is chosen by using FVSI method. Load flow has been carried out with optimal placement of TCSC and both system parameters (with and without TCSC) are compared. The overall cost function has been minimized using genetic algorithm (GA) optimization technique. Minimization of total cost which includes the TCSC installation cost and voltage deviation cost is considered as the objective function. The power loss with TCSC is reduced from 5.16 MW to 5.08 MW. The simulation is carried out using MATLAB environment.

articleTitle: Extraction and Optimization of Mathematical Knowledge Graph from Handwritten Math in Lecture Videos
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: Almost all existing techniques to do information retrieval from video containing handwritten mathematical expression, work on the static keyframe image extracted from the video. On the other hand, there is good progress in annotating video after converting it to a knowledge graph format. We combine both the techniques to achieve Mathematical Knowledge Graph (MKG) and optimize it to extract LATEX information to recognize mathematical expressions from the video at any point of time. Advantage of this technique is the consideration of the temporal aspect of the mathematical video. Additionally, this opens the paradigm of processing a mathematical video stream which is not prerecorded. Here we detect the discontinuation of ink-stoke in the video to process, recognize and add nodes to the MKG. Training for the classification of the mathematical symbol is done using the CHROME dataset and for typeset symbols, we used generated images.

articleTitle: A Multihypothesis Based Reconstruction Algorithm for Block Compressive Sensed WVSN Data
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: Wireless Visual Sensor Networks (WVSNs) have emerged as a prominent technological solution for surveillance and monitoring applications. These networks consist of smart camera sensor nodes, which intermittently capture video frames. These frames are then transmitted to a designated central node known as a sink. Block compressive sensing (BCS) for video compression is a research area that focuses on developing efficient algorithms for compressing video data by exploiting the sparsity of video signals in spatial and temporal domains. The primary goal of BCS-based techniques is to reduce the storage and bandwidth requirements of video data while maintaining acceptable video quality. The associated lightweight encoders and the demand for very less storage space make them suitable for WVSN applications where energy, bandwidth, and storage resources are limited. Reconstruction algorithms play a vital role in maintaining image quality and a prominent one such algorithm is Smooth Projected Landweber (SPL). This paper evaluates the appropriateness of an iterative multihypothesis SPL-based reconstruction strategy in WVSN data aggregation.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Slotted Antenna Array for Vehicular Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: Dedicated short-range communication (DSRC) and vehicle to everything communications are now is the key research area as there are numerous internet of things (1oT) applications and to ensure road safety. As there is a limited space available on the vehicles to mount the antennas therefore it is necessary to embed multifunctional antennas and this requirement can only be fulfilled by low profile patch antennas. This paper presents the design of slotted antenna array operating at 5.8 GHz in C-band for DSRC and WLAN applications and it also resonate at 9.8 GHz for vehicle to satellite, Satellite-borne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) and radio navigation applications. After simulations, the design is fabricated and the simulated and measured reflection coefficient agree well.

articleTitle: Advanced UWB MIMO Antenna with Wide Bandwidth and High-Efficiency Performance for 5G
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: This article introduces an advanced Ultra-Wideband (UWB) Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) antenna characterized by its wide impedance bandwidth ranging from 24 GHz to 42.5 GHz. Designed with two rectangular microstrip elements, the antenna is built on a Rogers RT/Duroid 5880 dielectric substrate, precisely measuring $31 \times 11 \times 0.8$ mm$^{3}$. Utilizing an insect-feed feeding strategy, this design is particularly suited for a wide bandwidth, making it ideal for mm-Wave 5G communication technologies. simulations have shown that the antenna maintains mutual coupling between ports lower than -21.2 dB, a key indicator of its effective performance in a MIMO system. The antenna’s performance features include an Envelope Correlation Coefficient (ECC) of less than 0.004, diversity gain of up to 9.99 dB, and a high efficiency rate of 93% across its entire operational band. Furthermore, the antenna exhibits omnidirectional radiation patterns with a maximum gain of 5.56 dBi and stable total active reflection coefficient (TARC) attributes, enhancing its applicability in modern communication environments.

articleTitle: CMViT OCR: printed Indian language recognition using CMViT
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: In this research, we propose to recognize scanned line images of printed text in 11 Indian languages using CMViT, a single visual model created by merging ConvMixer with modified attention in Vision Transformer (SVTR). Recognizing the Indian language is challenging due to many reasons like cursive, making new shapes after joining in case of syllables, etc. There is also a similarity in some characters in Indian language scripts. Optical Character Recognition (OCR) is the science of recognizing and converting printed line images into analyzable, editable, and searchable forms. OCR has many use cases related to text extraction from scanned documents, handwritten documents, and scene text images. The research has been going on for the last decade by using artificial intelligence/machine learning tools to automatically analyze printed documents by converting them to editable digital text. Initially, AI-based OCR development started from RNN, LSTM, BiLSTM, and encoder-decoder architecture. The OCR is developed for 11 Indian languages named Bangla, Gujarati, Gurumukhi, Hindi, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Oriya, Tamil, Telugu, Urdu, and 2 bilinguals named Hindi-English, and Marathi-English. The OCR CER for each language is in the range of 0.15% to 1.95% using the proposed network.

articleTitle: Fault Emulation in Digital Circuits using FPGA based Software-Hardware Co-Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: This paper presents a semi-automated framework for emulation of single stuck-at faults in combinational circuits. The proposed fault emulation framework is established with the help of software-hardware co-simulation employing an ARM-SoC and an FPGA. This work also gives an emphasis on devising a C++ based EDA tool which aids in an automatic generation of fault injectable module required for the purpose of fault emulation. The efficacy of the proposed framework is verified through fault emulation of ISCAS’85 benchmark circuits, namely, C17, C432, C1355 and C1908. The test patterns used for emulation are obtained from commonly known open source ATPG tool ‘ATALANTA’ and the fault emulation results for each Circuit under Test (CUT) are compared with that obtained using ‘HOPE’ simulator. As the complexity of the CUT increases in terms of number of gates, the number of faults to be emulated also increase. The proposed scheme facilitates the provision for applying as many test patterns as the test engineer wants. However, the emulation of faults runs serially. The proposed approach is able to detect the circuit nodes stuck-at high or low voltages through fault emulation. Fault emulation results show that the number of test patterns required for fault testing of C1908 is lesser than that of C1355. However, the number of modelled faults for C1908 is greater than that of C1355. Most importantly, the proposed fault emulation framework poses a merely negligible FPGA resource overhead while achieving a speed up in fault detection over traditional computer simulation techniques.

articleTitle: Ensembling is all you need? Evaluating machine learning models on predicting the energy imbalance of prosumers
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: Energy imbalance is a situation where there is a mismatch between the expected energy consumption and energy production. Such energy imbalances cause widespread problems in the energy grid, sometimes causing instability of the grid leading to major grid failures. Prosumers, who both consume and produce energy, are one of the main contributors to the issue of energy imbalance. This paper presents a thorough investigation of different machine-learning algorithms for predicting the energy consumption and production behavior of prosumers in Estonia. Linear regression, MLP, TabNet, XGboost, LightGBM, and VotingRegressor-based ensemble of them are compared against each other. While individually, the LightGBM model performed best on this dataset with an MAE of 74.56, overall the VotingRegressor ensemble was the best-performing model with an MAE of 70.16. An investigation into the relative importance of predictive features is presented by exploring the feature importance of the trained LightGBM model. We also propose a target normalization pipeline to handle out-of-bound (OOB) inference issues, which resulted in a significant improvement in the performance of treebased models by an average of 7% on the test set.

articleTitle: Finding Homogeneous Collections in Aerial Object Detection Datasets
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: Object detection in remote sensing imagery leads to a geo-tagged set of detected objects. Multiple images collected over adjacent region depict the collection of objects for large spatial areas. This work intends to find interesting collections of a single class, i.e., homogeneous, such as a vehicle lot, a terminal of storage tanks, a chain of railway cars, etc., across such geospatial imagery. Finding collections in remote sensing can be useful in urban planning, traffic control, disaster management, etc. This study defines the problem and focuses on exploring techniques for finding patterns of such collections, demonstrating its utility through available datasets such as xView and FAIR1M.

articleTitle: Low-Cost Method of Noise Estimation for Image and Video Coding
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: Existing video and image codecs exploit spatial and temporal correlation to achieve compression, but presence of noise reduces this correlation and hence adversely effects their compression efficiency. Noise filtering of the input signal can significantly improve compression efficiency of video encoders. Temporal noise filtering is one such technique that can improve the compression efficiency of encoding noisy content by 5-10% with an AVI reference encoder. Temporal filtering relies on motion information and noise estimation for generating accurate filter coefficients. Generally, encoders have motion estimation modules which can be used for getting motion information, but noise estimation requires a special implementation. In this proposal, we present a low-cost noise estimation method which is used with temporal filtering in AV1 encoding. We calculate the difference between pixels in horizontal and vertical directions to generate the histograms of a difference map. A simple analysis of these histograms provides a very accurate measure of variance of the noise in frames. In comparison to the existing methods, this method has a very low computational overhead.

articleTitle: Improved Performance of Oppositely Doped CoreShell Junctionless Nanowire FET Using Gate Material Engineering
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: The impact of work function variation on Dual Material Gate Oppositely Doped Core-Shell Junctionless Nanowire FET (DMG-ODCS-JLNWFET) is explored in this paper. The variation in surface potential, electric field, band energy, drain current $(\mathrm {I_{D}})$, leakage current $(\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{O}\mathrm{F}\mathrm{F}})$, subthreshold slope (SS), transconductance $(\mathrm{g}_{\mathrm{m}})$, and switching ratio $(\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{O}\mathrm{N}}/\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{O}\mathrm{F}\mathrm{F}})$ are analyzed. The performance of DMG-ODCS-JLNWFET is also compared with Single Material Gate (SMG) ODCS-JLNWFET. The results demonstrate that the proposed device shows significant advancements, boasting improvements of 18.9%, 73.7%, 26.8%, and 10.8% in $\mathrm {I_{D}}$, $\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{O}\mathrm{F}\mathrm{F}}, \mathrm{g}_{\mathrm{m}}$, and SS respectively when compared to SMG-ODCS-JLNWFET. These noteworthy enhancements underscore the device’s exceptional suitability for both analog and digital applications within the confines of nano-scale dimensions.

articleTitle: Decoding Image Integrity: A Comprehensive Analysis of YOLOv8’s Performance for Detecting Copy-Move Forgery
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: Copy-move forgery represents a prevalent type of image manipulation wherein a segment of an image is duplicated and inserted into another area within the same image. Its primary intent is to deceive viewers or alter the image’s content. Detecting such alterations is pivotal in upholding the integrity and authenticity of digital images. In this research, we undertook the task of training the YOLOv8 image classification model using our extensive image forensics dataset. Additionally, we leveraged Gradio to develop a user-friendly graphical interface, streamlining the detection process. The proposed methodology unfolds in two distinct phases: the training of the YOLOv8 model and the creation of a user-friendly interface using Gradio. To validate our model’s performance, we conducted training and validation on a combined dataset created from MICC-F220, MICC-F600, and MICC-F2000 datasets. Furthermore, we assessed the model’s generalization capability by subjecting it to the CoMoFoD v2 dataset. The experimental results substantiate the model’s efficacy, revealing an impressive accuracy of 97% with a mere 0.030 error rate, achieved within a concise span of 10 training epochs. These outcomes underscore the practical utility and robustness of our proposed framework.

articleTitle: Enhanced Cardiovascular Risk Prediction Using ML Powered Web Application
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: This paper discusses a machine learning (ML) application tailored for predicting heart disease risk, examining different models that are efficient in risk assessment. Our study encompasses the comprehensive implementation of various Machine learning algorithms as well as their comparison, including decision trees, random forests, logistic regression, support vector machines, and neural networks. The chosen ML model is then deployed through a web application, prioritizing a user-friendly platform towards ensuring public accessibility. Our results underscore the remarkable efficacy of ML in precisely forecasting specific risk of heart diseases and thus its web deployment enhances its potential and opens it up to a larger audience. Moreover, our findings advocate for the seamless integration of advanced machine learning methods within health risk assessment frameworks. In essence, this research highlights that, by leveraging sophisticated algorithms and prioritizing accessibility, we aim to propel the adoption of ML-powered solutions in healthcare, ultimately fostering proactive health management and preventive care initiatives.

articleTitle: Modeling Blockchain For Different Industries in Developing Economy
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: Blockchain technology is one of the building blocks of smart technologies that are finding their way in different industries across the globe. The different applications of blockchain technology in telecommunication, finance, food safety and security, medical, and maritime, is briefly discussed in ordEr to envisage the potential of this technology to reshape the industries. This facilitates the researchers to develop the initial idea of the application of blockchain in their area of interest. DEMATEL technique is used to model the blockchain artifacts for each industry. It is concluded that blockchain technology has its vast application to enhance the security, traceability and transparency in different industries.

articleTitle: Linear Parameter Varying Model-Based Predictive Trajectory Tracking Control of Quadrotor
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: This paper incorporates a constrained Model Predictive Control (MPC) formulation for attitude control of an F450 Quadrotor that has potential of Linear Parameter Varying (LPV) modeling of the attitude subsystem to consider the change in system dynamics. The proposed non-simplified LPV-MPC problem has been solved using Quadratic Programming, while the MPC prediction model has been manipulated to update the system dynamics. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the trajectory tracking capabilities of the non-simplified LPV-MPC controller over its simplified counterpart.

articleTitle: Design of 8×8 Phased Array Antenna for Sub-6 GHz 5G Automotive Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: 5G provides the enhanced channel capacity, extended coverage and reliable connection for the user terminal for both terrestrial and non-terrestrial automotive communications. Phased array antenna with beamforming capability is prominent solution to maintain the connection in the moving vehicle. This paper describes and analyze the 8$\times$8 asymmetric U-slot patch antenna array along with beamforming capability. The design resonates at 3.5 GHz which is the part of sub-6 GHz frequency band dedicated for 5G wireless communication. The proposed array provides the gain of 22.7 dB which ensures the significant improvement in data rate according to link budget calculations. The beamforming feature of the proposed design demonstrates the ±30° beam shift with the scan angle of ±40°. The performance parameters of the proposed design are suitable for various automotive wireless use cases.

articleTitle: Design a Compact and Flexible Spiral Antenna for Superficial Tumors Treatment
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: In this paper, a compact and flexible spiral antenna is designed for superficial tumor treatment having different shapes and sizes. The proposed antenna consists of a spiral radiating patch with a coplanar waveguide feed. The antenna is designed on FR4 substrate having a thickness is 0.15 mm and a size of the antenna is 18 × 19 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The performance of a flexible spiral antenna (FSA) is tested in the presence of a heterogeneous phantom (skin, fat, and muscle) and also with a replicate of the human model (Voxel model). The bending effect of FSA is studied with a voxel model. The performance of FSA is evaluated in terms of specification absorption rate (SAR), and relative parameters of SAR i.e. penetration depth (PD) and effective field size (EFS). The performance of FSA is also analyzed for inserting different shapes and sizes of superficial tumors in the phantom and also studied the steady state and transient state temperature distribution in the phantom and gustav model.

articleTitle: Performance Improvement of Hybrid RoF and RoFSO System under High Atmospheric Turbulence
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: RoF and RoFSO are emerging as technologies of interest to generate millimeter (mm) waves in optical domain and to provide solutions for access networks in 5G and 6G mobile services. There are different mm wave frequency bands, which have been standardized or in process of standardization for different applicatuions. This paper analyses the performance of propagation of 60 GHz mm-wave frequency over hybrid radio over fiber (RoF) and radio over free space optic (RoFSO) system under high atmospheric turbulence. The 60 GHz mm-wave frequency is generated in the optical domain using an analog approach of optical double sideband (ODSB) with partial carrier suppression (PCS). The RoF is used to extend the transmission reach and RoFSO for last-mile connectivity or access network. This paper also explores the use of non-return to zero inverted (NRZI) source encoding in improving the performance of the considered system under high atmospheric turbulence. A comparison of different edge shapes of NRZ and RZ modulation formats has also been explored.

Author Keywords: edge shapes of NRZ and RZ pulses

articleTitle: Enhanced Hair Disease Classification Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: The abstract summarizes the important findings & results of this research study, which focuses on the categorization of various hair conditions with a machine-learning model. Precision, recall, and F1-Score metrics for many hair illness classes, like Alopecia Areata, Tinea Capitis, Telogen Effluvium, Scarring Alopecia, Trichotillomania, Folliculitis, Head Lice, or Psoriasis, are quite promising. various metrics demonstrate the model’s abilities to reliably categorize various diseases, with accuracy values fluctuating between 88.04% to 88.89% and recall values continuously falling in the range from 87.80% to 89.19%. To evaluate the performance of this model, they used a dataset of 8550 photos. Notably, the model achieved an amazing total accuracy of 88.53%, demonstrating its ability to perform picture categorization tasks. The balanced Fl scores, which range from 88.02% to 88.99%, illustrate the model’s ability to achieve a harmonious trade-off between precision and recall. The model’s overall efficacy in classifying hair illnesses is highlighted by the macro average F1-Score of88.53%, and the weighted average F1-Score at 88.54% due to class imbalances, validating its uniform high-performance measures. Its consistent and high-performance characteristics across all classes are shown by the micro average F1-Score of88.54%. With an overall accuracy of 97%, this study demonstrates the model’s dependability and efficacy in the detection and categorization of a wide range of hair problems.

articleTitle: NeuroSyght: An AI-Powered Approach on Emotion Classification from EEG Data
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: The perception and interpretation of emotions are crucial to understand human behavior and cognition, which has far-reaching implications in different disciplines, including mental health diagnosis and human-computer interaction. This study is focused on the construction of a robust model capable of predicting emotions based on electroencephalogram (EEG) signals. EEG data, when harnessed through the power of artificial intelligence, has the potential to be a significant resource. The result of this research is NeuroSyght, a meticulously crafted custom model based on the architecture of a 1-dimensional (1-D) convolutional neural network. Proposed model is designed to adeptly capture the distinctive attributes of 1-D signals, particularly those derived from EEG brainwaves using the dataset SEED-V. The model effortlessly navigates the intricacies involved in mapping the nuanced features corresponding to the elicited emotions it represents. NeuroSyght stands as an exemplar to show the harmonious integration of advanced neural network design with the intricate interpretation of EEG data, presenting a refined and effective novel approach to emotion prediction. The model demonstrates an extraordinary accuracy of 99.97% when applied to the collected differential entropy features from the SEED-V dataset. This exception al precision highlights the credibility and promise of the proposed paradigm.

articleTitle: Revitalizing ancient murals in the Shekhawati region through image inpainting techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: India has an extensive range of ancient artistic expressions in the form of mural paintings. These murals incorporate architectural features representing the cultural heritage of ancient civilizations. These paintings have declined over time due to human negligence and have deteriorated. The traditional approaches to restore this significant artwork are less effective and have been declared impotent. Thus, a practical digital inpainting framework is suggested to breathe new life into degraded murals. The suggested framework employs a two-step approach to attain optimal results in reconstructing murals for restoration purposes. In the first step, a semantic model is utilized to generate damage, defining masks that serve as inpainting parameters in various instances. The second step evaluates the effectiveness of three distinct inpainting architectures: PCONV, Conditional Texture Structure Dual Generation, and T-former.Additionally, this study provides a qualitative and quantitative comparison, utilizing metrics such as style loss, perceptual loss, SSIM, PSNR, and the perceptual quality of completeness. The results of the comparative analysis reveal that the T-former model outperforms others significantly, attaining an average SSIM of 0.9947 and a PSNR score of 45.3815 on test images. Moreover, the experiment’s reconstruction, achieved by constraining all patches, successfully passes the visual inspection test, faithfully replicating the original mural.

articleTitle: Empirical study of deep reinforcement learning algorithms for CartPole problem
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: CartPole problem is a classical control problem, which is important in many fields, including robotics and self-driving cars. Deep reinforcement learning is applied for controlling the CartPole balancing problem. This study compares the performance of four deep reinforcement learning algorithms: Deep Q-Network (DQN), Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), QR (Quantile Regression) DQN, and Advantage Actor-Critic (A2C). The CartPole balance problem in the OpenAIGym environment is taken into consideration to execute the deep reinforcement learning algorithms. Many deep Reinforcement algorithms exist, and selecting the right one might be difficult depending on the problem’s characteristics. Our findings can help in the ranking of the four methods based on how well they fit the requirements of a given application. The performance in terms of training time, training timesteps, maximum value of episode-reward-mean, and average frames per second for each method are evaluated. The results demonstrate that the best approach for resolving this problem is to use PPO method with a set of prespecified hyperparameters.

articleTitle: Document Image Script Identification using Deep Network
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: In this paper, we propose script identification of Indian language document images using MobileNetV3. Script identification at the page level is an essential task for Optical Character Recognition (OCR). OCR is a time-consuming task with a lot of computation required. To make an accurate, fast, and efficient script identification module, we have employed MobileNetV3, a mobile and CPU-friendly Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) algorithm. MobileNetV3 results are comparable to ResNet50 on the ImageNet dataset. The methodology addresses challenges in real-world scenarios, enhancing robustness. The paper demonstrates the classification of six Indian scripts (Bangla, Gurumukhi, Hindi, Kannada, Malayalam, and Tamil) and English. Four experiments have been performed. The first experiment uses MobileNetV3 with center loss (CL) and without skew detection (no angle). The second experiment uses MobileNetV3 without CL and skew detection (no angle). The third experiment is done by modifying MobileNetV3 with CL and without skew. The fourth experiment uses MobileNetV3 with CL and skew angle detection (range −10 to 10 degrees). The accuracy of the fourth experiment is 96% with skew detection. The best experiment is the first, which uses CL and cross-entropy loss and achieves an impressive accuracy of 98%.

articleTitle: ShaveNet: Facial hair removal preprocessing framework for Face and Visual-Speech biometrics
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: Face and Visual-Speech biometric systems accuracy is affected by the presence and absence of facial hair. The proposed ShaveNet, a deep learning approach, aims to remove facial hair from the lower half of facial images to assist Face and Visual-Speech (VS) biometric systems. Leveraging Cycle-Consistent Generative Adversarial Network (Cycle GAN), offers a promising framework for facial hair removal compared to state-of-the-art conventional facial hair removal algorithms. The Cycle GAN can perform image-to-image translation by mapping the facial-hair image domain to the no-facial-hair image domain without requiring paired input-domain and output-domain image samples. The framework was trained using facial-hair and no-facial-hair mapping datasets constructed by combining the Beard-Face dataset, PGU-Face dataset and the Male-Celebrity-Face dataset collected from the web. The training image pairs were augmented to increase the number of training samples. The trained framework was tested on a virtual barber beard dataset and male celebrity beard images downloaded from the web. The results revealed that the Cycle GAN is preferable to conventional methods for facial hair removal, achieving high SSIM, PSNR, and low FID scores.

articleTitle: Comparative study of YOLOv8 and YOLO-NAS for agriculture application
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: Agricultural tasks have significantly improved as a result of ongoing machine learning (ML) improvements. Deep learning (DL), which has a significant capacity for extracting high-dimensional features from fruit images, is widely applied to the automated detection and harvesting of fruits. In the fields of fruit recognition and automated harvesting, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have demonstrated the ability to attain speed and accuracy levels that rival human performance. This article compares the performance of YOLOv8m with YOLO-NASl for grapes detection. In this research, the YOLOv8 and YOLO-nas object detection models, including their different scales, were trained using a publicly available Embrapa WGISD dataset. The dataset consists of 300 digital images of grapes growing in vineyard settings, and it includes a total of 4,432 annotations. The performance of the YOLOv8m and YOLO-NASl model were evaluated using metrics such as recall, precision, and the mean average precision (mAP@50). In the subset of test data, YOLOv8m achieved the top overall performance, with a precision (0.855), mAP@50 (0.885), and recall (0.827), while best recall was obtained from YOLO-NASl (0.934).

articleTitle: Multi-Modal Data Fusion Based Cardiac Disease Prediction using Late Fusion and 2D CNN Architectures
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: This paper presents a multimodal data based late fusion technique used in the classification of cardiac normality and abnormality integrating 12-lead ECG image data and electronic health records (EHR) data. Cardiac diseases are big problems worldwide, and need better ways to diagnose to help patients. Only electrocardiograms (ECG) report may not be conclusive for predicting cardiac normality and abnormality. In recent studies, the integration of ECG image and EHR has emerged as a promising approach for improving cardiac disease detection and diagnosis. The EHR data includes critical parameters such as Blood Pressure (BP), Oxygen Saturation (SpO2), Body Mass Index (BMI), and blood sugar level etc. These parameters are obtained along with 12-lead ECG images, from our own prepared multimodal database (CardioHTDC database). The proposed multimodal late fusion technique employs a deep learning architecture. The late fusion technique involves concatenating the outputs of individual deep learning architecture to create a combined feature vector that incorporates both visual and structured information. A 2D CNN (Convolutional Neural Network) architecture is considered as model I, responsible for feature extraction from 12-lead ECG images while an MLP (Multi-Layer Perceptron) architecture is designated as model II, tasked with processing EHR data, to capture patterns, that help predicting early cardiac disease. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed late fusion technique provides significant important by achieving a maximum accuracy for cardiac multimodal dataset, while an accuracy of only 72.2% has achieved using multimodal late fusion techniques. However, lower accuracy of the algorithms is multi-modal cardiac dataset and non-availability of the other existing dataset.

articleTitle: Enhancing IoT Ecosystems through Effective Master Data Management
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: This study explores the quantitative impact of Master Data Management (MDM) implementation on Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystems.
